title: WoW Players Waited 6 Years to Set Foot on Mount Hyjal
hook: Mount Hyjal, where Warcraft III ended, stayed off limits for six years until Cataclysm opened it and sold 3.3 million copies in a day. Tomorrow it returns as an endgame zone in WoW: Forever. Are you logging in?
script: Did you know World of Warcraft players waited six years to set foot on Mount Hyjal? Hyjal is the mountain that holds the World Tree, where Archimonde was destroyed at the end of Warcraft Three. When World of Warcraft launched in two thousand four, that famous mountain was nowhere you could actually go. The closest anyone got was a time travel raid that replayed the old battle. Then, at BlizzCon in the summer of two thousand nine, Blizzard announced Cataclysm. Mount Hyjal was finally reopened as a real zone, with players entering by way of Moonglade. Cataclysm finally launched in December of twenty ten, and it sold more than three million copies on day one. This week that mountain matters again. World of Warcraft Forever goes live tomorrow, November fourth, as a third permanent version of the game beside modern WoW and Classic. It is included with a normal subscription. Forever stops at level sixty and uses the original continents, but Mount Hyjal is one of its new endgame zones. A twenty player raid called Hyjal Summit opens there on December ninth. So a mountain that stayed out of reach for six years is now back in a brand new version of the game. Are you logging into Forever tomorrow? Follow for more gaming history.
